attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors geometrically represents the product of the length of one vector and the projection of the other vector onto it. If vectors A and B have an angle θ between them, then A·B = |A||B|cosθ. When the vectors are orthogonal (θ = 90°), cosθ = 0, so their dot product is zero, indicating no projection of one onto the other. If the dot product is negative, it means the angle between the vectors is greater than 90°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, reflecting a negative component along that axis.
